ai-budget-in-gesture.note: AI is asked for only inside a click or key handler, never at load or on a timer: a replay counts grants refused no_gesture.

ai-disclosure-shown.note: The HUD draws ai.disclosure() once the game uses AI, and state().ai.disclosed reports it; a state with no ai status is unmeasured.

ai-handles-no-answer.note: With AI off every demo ends with no call left waiting, no crash and no console error: an optional game plays on its fallback, an AI-only one stops behind Studio's needs-AI state.

ai-no-direct-model-calls.note: The build names no AI vendor's API host and holds no vendor key: genex-ai is the only way to a model.

ai-output-clamped.note: The largest and smallest answers the game's schemas allow break nothing: the applier clamps numbers, cuts strings and drops unknown ids before an answer reaches the game.

ai-replay-deterministic.note: A game that uses play-time AI replays every demo from its saved playtest (ai/tapes/<demo>.jsonl) and reaches the same frames under seeds 1-3. The harness puts it on the entry owner's board when the plan declares ai.

ai-tape-covers-demos.note: Every AI call a demo makes is answered by its saved playtest; a call the tape has no line for, or a line the reader refuses, fails. Record again with ai_record after changing a prompt, a schema or a site.

camera-player-eye.note: A camera tagged player-eye exists in the graph, so the judge can be shown the frame the player sees. Where it points is the game's own decision — the follow-camera band is in camera.named-rig.

demo-walk.name: walk
demo-walk.note: The named config.demos entry "walk" (a short deterministic control script) runs to its end state without a console error. Optional: a game that registers no walk demo is unmeasured, not failed.

drawcalls-ceiling.note: The whole frame's honest figures from state().__render (counted at the graphics API, post pass included) stay under 1000 draw calls and 400k triangles; nothing countable is unmeasured, not failed.

player-moved.note: After the harness drives the game's own movement keys, state().player.x or .z changed; identical before and after means "the controls do not work". needs names the same paths delta() reads, so a build that reports no player — or one whose player only appears after the play script — is unmeasured, not passed.

primary-action-registers.note: state() reports actions.primary — a count of the game's main verb, whatever it is (a shot, a jump, a placed tile). The scripted controls trigger it, so the count must rise at least once.
